reason: Runnable (GF(2) bit-packed rank, <2 min at n<=13, structural quantities only: syzygy counts, Hilbert function, d_reg, d_F; no wall time). But predictions as written are mathematically wrong, so the test is not a valid discriminator. MEASURED here (homogeneous F_2[a,b], degree-3 syzygies = 2k*n - dim(I_3), n=5,7,9,11, k=ceil(n/2), 4 random V each): Moore/Semaev top forms give 0 linear syzygies at every n (not >=2n); random symmetric forms give 0 (6 on 1 of 4 seeds at n=5); random non-symmetric forms give 0 (6 on 1 of 4 seeds at n=5). Moore and random controls are indistinguishable. Cause: the Frobenius-collapse syzygy sum_j v_j a_j*(ab)^top = sigma(a)b needs a_j^2=a_j (Boolean reduction), which is non-homogeneous and is destroyed both in F_2[a,b] and in the quotient by a_j^2,b_l^2 (there y_i(a)^2=0, not y_{i+1}(a)). So prediction (1) is impossible in the proposed rings. Prediction (2) is also wrong: V(I^top) needs S,T subset of [n], S union T=[n], each |S|,|T|<=k-1 (nonzero a killed by |S| independent Moore forms needs |S|<=k-1), so n=2k-1 gives EMPTY zero set (count 0, not C(2k,k)=70); the finite case is n=2k-2 with C(2k-2,k-1) points. But a generic complete intersection of 2k-2 (1,1)-forms on P^{k-1} x P^{k-1} has the same bidegree count C(2k-2,k-1), so the n=2k-2 point count does not separate Moore from generic. The enumeration arithmetic is off by 1e6 (|P^3(F_128)|=(2^28-1)/(2^7-1)=2113665, pairs 4.5e12, infeasible; use linear algebra over F_{2^n} per support pair instead). Null arm (4) 'n random F_2-rational products l_i(a)m_i(b)' is the wrong null: Moore forms are symmetric (Tr(delta ab) symmetric in a,b) and only K-rational individually, so the control must be random symmetric F_2 bilinear forms and/or random K-conjugate-orbit products. Genericity assumption 'any k of n Moore forms independent' is false for arbitrary row subsets of the Moore matrix at toy n (only consecutive-row minors are guaranteed); needs per-V check. Scaling to n=131: claims are (n,k)-structural so they would transfer IF a closed form / proof exists; toy n<=13 data alone cannot certify behaviour at n=131 and k~n/2 is not the programme's regime (l/n small). Result is theory-class: no B*D^2 change, so toy outcome cannot move the non-genericity line.
fix: Redesign (all python3 GF(2) elimination, <5 CPU-min): (A) Work with the actual non-homogeneous Boolean system from ffd_semaev_core.build_system at prime n in {7,11,13}, l=k in 3..6: count linear syzygies at degree 3 as 2k*n_eqs-style rank deficiency of {x*f} reduced mod a_j^2=a_j,b_l^2=b_l, versus (i) random_matched null from ffd_semaev_core and (ii) random symmetric bilinear forms with same (n,k) lifted with the same Frobenius-collapse-free random affine parts; the Frobenius syzygy exists only here. Report counts as exact integers. (B) Homogeneous top-form ideal: replace prediction with measured 0 syzygies at degree 3 and measure first nonzero Betti/linear-syzygy degree and Hilbert function H(d) d<=7 for Moore vs random symmetric forms vs random K-conjugate products; the idea survives only if H differs from the random symmetric null and is V-independent across >=5 V at fixed (n,k). (C) Zero set: use n=2k-2 (e.g. n=6,k=4 or n=10,k=6; composite n allowed only as a count check), count K-rational points by solving kernels of k-1 Moore rows per support S (linear algebra, no enumeration), expect C(2k-2,k-1) for Moore AND for generic (no discrimination: drop it as a falsifier, keep as a sanity check); for n=2k-1 assert empty. (D) Record d_reg(F^top)+1 vs measured d_F (from fall_profile) per instance, and the per-V minor-nonvanishing check. Add a scaling note: any survivor must give H(n,k) in closed form and be checked at n=13..17 with k fixed 3..4 (the l<<n regime) before any statement about n=131.
